It also comes from `CHANGELOG.md`, which records adding the MIT license to the project and to every source file.

I did not use the claude-mem memory search results. They returned only bare one-line prompts such as "GPL-3.0" and "Apache-2.0", with no project, context or indication of which is current. They sit among unrelated prompts about bcrypt, tokio and calver, so they aren't project decisions. If you meant one of those to be the current decision, it isn't recorded anywhere in the repo, and the file would need to change.

The first shell attempt to create the file errored, so I wrote it with the Write tool instead. Nothing is committed.
